reasoning: Recent high-quality polling in the last 45 days shows Sherrod Brown with a mid- to high-single-digit lead in the 2026 Ohio Senate race, while there are no fresh, Ohio-specific presidential general-election polls in that window, so only the Senate race can be credibly quantified. The Fox News poll (summarized by multiple outlets) has Brown +8, and aggregators and analysts describe the overall race as effectively a toss-up but with Democrats holding a very small average edge of around 1 point, consistent with a Democratic-leaning but still highly competitive contest in a structurally Republican state (R+6 PVI).

sources.name: Cincinnati Enquirer (reporting Fox News poll)
sources.details: A Fox News poll of Ohio voters finds Sherrod Brown at 53% and Jon Husted at 45% in the 2026 Senate race, an 8-point Democratic lead, unchanged from a June poll.

sources.name: Washington Examiner (summarizing Fox News poll)
sources.details: Coverage of a Fox News poll notes Sherrod Brown maintaining an 8-point advantage over Jon Husted, 53% to 45%, in the Ohio Senate race, matching the previous Fox poll.

sources.name: Political Wire (on Fox News poll)
sources.details: A writeup describes a poll showing Sherrod Brown leading Jon Husted 53% to 45% in the Ohio Senate race, highlighting the 8-point gap and demographic splits.

sources.name: ElectionDesk.org (summarizing AARP poll)
sources.details: A June AARP-commissioned poll of 800 likely voters is reported as finding Sherrod Brown leading Jon Husted 48% to 45% in the Ohio Senate race, within the margin of error.

sources.name: G2G Consulting (polling average summary)
sources.details: A consulting brief states that polling averages in the Ohio Senate race show Sherrod Brown holding a razor-thin lead of about +0.6 points, with individual polls alternating slight advantages for each candidate.

sources.name: Idaho Public Press (summarizing VoteHub averages)
sources.details: An article reports that VoteHub’s July average moved the Ohio Senate race from a 0.3-point Republican edge in April to a 0.9-point Democratic edge in July, characterizing Democrats as narrowly ahead.

sources.name: CNN (Senate seats most likely to flip)
sources.details: A Senate race rankings piece describes the Ohio Senate contest as one of the most likely to flip, highlighting that Sherrod Brown continues to outraise Republican Sen. Jon Husted and that the race remains highly competitive, effectively a toss-up.

sources.name: Daily Kos (analysis of Ohio independents and Senate race)
sources.details: A political newsletter notes that available polling suggests the Ohio Senate race is either a dead heat or that Jon Husted is narrowly ahead by around three points, while also emphasizing how competitive the contest is in a conservative-leaning state.

sources.name: Thin Gold Glossary (Cook PVI explanation and values)
sources.details: A glossary-style piece explains that the Cook Partisan Voting Index is based on recent presidential results and indicates Ohio’s current statewide PVI, which shows the state leaning Republican by several points.
